correctness.rationale: Proposition 7.17 explicitly gives a normally presented ambient ring A, a quotient ideal J with J_m=0 for m<M, J_M nonzero, and J generated in degree M. For M>2, every relation of smaller degree lies in the ambient quadratic ideal, so it cannot generate an element whose class in J_M is nonzero; a degree-M minimal generator is forced. For M<=2, the anticanonical embedding is nondegenerate and has nonzero ideal, hence no degree-one generator but at least one degree-two generator. Together with the published upper bound this proves the claimed equality with all quantifiers and boundary cases stated.

value.rationale: The invariant t1 is the numerical input used by the initiating paper's automorphism-extension criterion. Showing that the family-wide upper bound is always attained identifies the exact first-relation complexity rather than another estimate. The result is uniform over all smooth positive-dimensional Fano hypersurfaces in products of projective spaces and separates the intrinsic sharpness of t1 from the sufficiency of downstream automorphism criteria.
